## Phase 0 — Verify the metal (locked)

### F-001 — GS alpha is a 0..128 domain: 0x80 is opaque, not 0xFF

**Measured:** Blend is Cv = (Cs-Cd)*As>>7 + Cd. Corroborated on the shipped blob: 0 of 513 probe-screen TEXQUAD channels exceed 0x80, so 0x80 -> 255 under modulate is exact rather than a clamp.

**Instrument:** `docs/bringup.md`

**Falsifier:** A TEXQUAD at As=0x80 that composites to anything but full coverage

**Rests on this:** F-002

Art authored at 255 alpha asks for about twice the coverage it has.

*#28*

### F-002 — gsKit's default ALPHA runs the blend backwards

**Measured:** Default GS_BLEND_BACK2FRONT (0x01) gives A=Cd B=Cs C=As D=Cs, i.e. effective coverage 128-As. Solved back from each rendered ladder swatch on a SCPH-50000 and under Play!, exact on every rung. 0x40 was the only clean rung -- the single alpha where 128-As == As -- which a frame that merely "looked wrong" would never have singled out.

**Instrument:** `docs/bringup.md`

**Falsifier:** A default-state blend where coverage tracks As rather than 128-As

**Depends on:** [F-001](#f-001) (GS alpha is a 0..128 domain: 0x80 is opaque, not…)

Two corollaries that cost time. The fix must run EVERY FRAME, because GS blend state is global and survives your frame: an early two-ladder capture showed both ladders clean because the fix persisted into frame 2 and the test was comparing itself against itself. And it must go through gsKit_set_primalpha -- assigning gs->PrimAlpha does not emit the register, which was identified by two ladders coming back byte-identical.

*#28, #30*

### F-003 — A misaligned DMA source is truncated, not faulted

**Measured:** A GIF DMA_REF tag's ADDR field starts at bit 4, so a source under 16-byte alignment cannot be expressed and the transfer begins up to 15 bytes early. off_blob mod 16 was 4, 12, 4, 4 across four shipped blobs; 12 bytes is 12 texels of a 256-wide PSMT8 atlas. Fixing it produced the first green ground-truth emulator diff in the project's history, RMSE 22.89 -> 4.79.

**Instrument:** `docs/format-uib.md`

**Falsifier:** A blob with off_blob mod 16 != 0 whose textures land correctly

The operator reported "the right edge of every image butted against its left edge" twice, and it was read past twice. Because the truncation lives in the DMA tag format rather than in silicon, Play! reproduced both the fault and the fix.

*#40*

### F-004 — PrimAlphaEnable is one field driving two registers: PRIM.ABE and TEX0.TCC

**Measured:** Passed in the tcc position at all 30 GS_SETREG_TEX0 sites, read per draw at all 65 reads, never latched. TCC=0 tells the GS the glyph atlas is opaque RGB, so every glyph becomes a solid block of its own text colour.

**Instrument:** `runtime/ps2ui.c`

**Falsifier:** A build with PrimAlphaEnable off whose glyphs keep their antialiasing

Produces the signature "text broken, boxes fine", because glyph coverage IS texture alpha while untextured geometry is unaffected.

*#39*

### F-005 — gsKit has no DECAL path; TEX0.TFX is hardcoded to MODULATE

**Measured:** GSTEXTURE has no Function field at 43122eb, and TFX is 0 at all 30 TEX0 sites. TEX0.TBW is also unsettable by the caller: gsKit_texture_upload's first statement is gsKit_setup_tbw().

**Instrument:** `runtime/vendor/gsKit/gsTexture.h`

**Falsifier:** A GSTEXTURE field or gsKit call that selects DECAL

Settled by reading the library, after four bench-blocking questions in a row -- GSTEXTURE::Function, TEX0.TFX, TEX0.TCC, TEX0.TBW -- were all answerable from source and were instead attacked with A/B ELFs on a console. See L-012.

*#38, #39*

### F-006 — gsKit's TexManager cannot report VRAM exhaustion; it hangs

**Measured:** _blockAlloc loops evicting ever-hotter textures until something fits and has no NULL-returning exit, so an over-budget blob under raw TexManager_bind is a console hang inside gsKit rather than an error code.

**Instrument:** `runtime/ps2ui.c`

**Falsifier:** An over-budget bind that returns an error instead of hanging

Hence ps2ui keeps an all-or-nothing preflight AND re-checks per frame, because every gsKit_vram_alloc resets the manager's block list and shrinks the region the preflight approved.

*#41*

### F-011 — A +0.5 UV bias is wrong: under NEAREST at 1:1 it lands one texel past target ~~overturned~~

**Measured:** Pixel i of a 1:1 sprite centres at x0+i+0.5, so u = u0+i+0.5, which floors to u0+i. Adding 0.5 gives u0+i+1.

**Instrument:** `docs/bringup.md`

**Falsifier:** A renderer where a +0.5 bias does not move the sampled texel

**Overturned by:** [F-020](#f-020) (Both texture axes lose their last texel independ…)

KEPT DELIBERATELY, AND STILL TRUE OF EVERY RENDERER HERE EXCEPT THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The arithmetic is correct for an exact interpolator; the premise -- that the GS is one -- is not. It survived months because at power-of-two spans it is exactly right, and because the previewer and Play! both compute in float with no reciprocal, so every host-side renderer this project owns agreed with it. Nothing off-console could have caught it.

*#36, #57*

### F-012 — gsKit_texture_upload does not write the data cache back, so the GS reads stale palette memory ~~overturned~~

**Measured:** Believed from reading the narrow symbol. Disproved by reading one line further: gsKit_texture_send opens with an unconditional FlushCache(0) on every path (gsTexture.c:266), so no cache fault ever occurred.

**Instrument:** `docs/bringup.md`

**Falsifier:** A flush on the upload path, which there is

**Overturned by:** [F-013](#f-013) (gsKit flushes the whole data cache inside its tr…)

Kept because of HOW it died. The disproving line was in the author's own grep output, one line above the hits quoted -- "I searched for the narrow symbol and stopped reading." The explicit SyncDCache calls stayed as hardening rather than being reverted, so the code no longer depends on that implementation detail either way.

*#41*

## Phase 1 — One resource model (locked)

### F-019 — The GS is not an exact UV interpolator

**Measured:** Bench S8, SCPH-50000: a textured sprite h pixels tall sampling h texels keeps its last texel row only at h in {1,2,4,8} -- exactly the heights where 1/h is exact in binary. The same rungs drawn as stacked untextured quads keep every row, so the rasteriser and the display are not involved.

**Instrument:** `runtime/sample/ladder_pattern.h`

**Falsifier:** A non-power-of-two span that keeps its last texel row with no bias, or an untextured stack that loses one

**Rests on this:** F-020, F-021, F-022

The mechanism -- a reciprocal in the per-scanline UV step -- remains a HYPOTHESIS. The correction is measured; the explanation is not.

*#56, #58*

### F-020 — Both texture axes lose their last texel independently, each on its own span

**Measured:** Bench S10, SCPH-50000: blocks 100 wide, heights 1-12. At bias 0 the last ROW is lost unless the height is a power of two, and the last COLUMN is always lost because 100 is not. The clincher is heights 4 and 8, which keep their row and still lose their column.

**Instrument:** `runtime/sample/ladder2_pattern.h`

**Falsifier:** A quad whose width is not a power of two that keeps its last column with no bias

**Depends on:** [F-019](#f-019) (The GS is not an exact UV interpolator…)

**Overturns:** [F-011](#f-011) (A +0.5 UV bias is wrong: under NEAREST at 1:1 it…)

**Rests on this:** F-021, F-022

Nothing before S10 could see the U axis: every earlier instrument was a power of two wide, which is the one span that cannot trigger the fault.

*#59, #61*

### F-021 — A 1/16 texel bias fixes the console and is a no-op on an exact renderer

**Measured:** floor(u + b + i + 0.5) == u + i for any b < 1/2, so every sub-half bias leaves an exact sampler on the same texel. 1/2 is the exact tipping point: a 1/2 build renders Library as Liibrarny and scores 17.34 on a frame diff whose healthy band is 4.79. The 1/16 build scored 4.79 / 13.73 -- the exact pre-bias value. 1/16 is also the smallest the GS's four fractional UV bits can express.

**Instrument:** `runtime/ps2ui.c`

**Falsifier:** An emulator diff that moves under 1/16, or a console span that still loses its last texel with it applied

**Depends on:** [F-020](#f-020) (Both texture axes lose their last texel independ…)

U is INFERRED, NOT MEASURED, at widths other than 100. Bench step S9 re-runs the real UI across dozens of genuine glyph widths and is the U sweep; it is also the only step that closes the defect, since everything so far tests the card rather than the shipping renderer.

*#61*

**Measured:** memcard atlases: size 13 has 113 inked glyphs, 74 of non-power-of-two width and 99 of non-power-of-two height; size 14 has 82 and 83. ps2ui-check prints this on every run.

**Instrument:** `packages/baker/ps2ui_bake/check.py`

**Falsifier:** A recount from the baked atlases that disagrees

**Depends on:** [F-020](#f-020) (Both texture axes lose their last texel independ…)

*#61*

### F-030 — wLaunchELF resets the IOP, so no launcher-loaded driver survives

**Measured:** Bench S6 returned "open cover0: -1" from a stick carrying four byte-verified 65,536-byte files. wLaunchELF launches via LoadExecPS2, which resets the IOP, so its USB drivers were gone before the ELF ran. Embedding the stack fixed it and S6 passed.

**Instrument:** `runtime/sample/main.c`

**Falsifier:** A launcher-loaded IRX still responding after LoadExecPS2

The USB stack is discovered rather than pinned: BDM in modern SDKs, usbhdfsd in older ones, both presenting mass:. CI refuses an empty module table.

*#55*

### F-031 — An OPL-class environment costs a 6,951-byte arena, not a 35,648-byte ceiling

**Measured:** opl-env: 6 screens, 125 slots, 246,032-byte blob, VRAM 392 KiB of a 736 KiB budget. The fixed-maxima context charged 35,648 bytes on every blob regardless of content; the 121-slot UC-3 fixture needs 8,285.

**Instrument:** `examples/opl-env/README.md`

**Falsifier:** A realistic environment whose arena exceeds the old fixed ceiling

**Rests on this:** F-032

## Phase 2 — Prove it with the OPL-class app (**open**)

### F-032 — Per-row reservations make a one-row scroll re-upload every cover *(provisional)*

**Measured:** Reservations are per ROW, not per item, so scrolling by one row leaves every visible row showing a different title: 9 x 3,136 = 28,224 bytes of upload per scroll step.

**Instrument:** `examples/opl-env/window.h`

**Falsifier:** A scroll step measured on hardware that uploads less than every row

**Depends on:** [F-031](#f-031) (An OPL-class environment costs a 6,951-byte aren…)

Arithmetic, not yet a measurement -- it needs the driver ELF and a sitting. Phase 3's likely answer is to rotate which reservation a row draws from rather than re-upload, and the number exists so that is decided by measurement rather than guessed.
